stanzas: اَلشَّبَابُ لَنْ يَكِلَّ هَمُّهُ أَنْ يَسْتَقِلَّ
نَسْتَقِي مِنَ الرَّدَىٰ وَلَنْ نَكُونَ لِلْعِدَىٰ
اَلْحُسَامُ وَ الْيَرَاعُ لَا الْكَلَامُ وَالنِّزَاعُ
مَجْدُنَا وَ عَهْدُنَا وَوَاجِبٌ مِنَ الْوَفَاء
orig.credit: Ibrahim Tuqan (c. 1934); the Arabic text as quoted in Wikipedia's article

stanzas: majesty and beauty, radiance and splendour
are in your hills, in your hills;
life and deliverance, delight and hope
are in your air, in your air.
Shall I see you, shall I see you
safe, living in ease, victorious and honoured?
Shall I see you in your height
the youth will not tire; their care is that you be independent
or they perish, or they perish.
We will drink of death, and we will not be to the enemies
We do not want, we do not want
our everlasting humiliation and our embittered life;
we do not want it, but we will bring back
our ancient glory, our ancient glory.
the sword and the pen, not talk and quarrelling,
Our glory and our covenant, and a duty of faithfulness,
is an aim that brings honour and a banner that flutters.
O how happy you are in your height,
overpowering your enemies, overpowering your enemies.
Al-shabābu lan yakilla hammuhu an yastaqilla
Nastaqī mina al-radá wa-lan nakūna lil-ʿidá

notes: Romanization: ALA-LC without the dots under letters (h, s, t, d, z for the emphatic letters), with ʿ for ʿayn and ʾ for hamza; the pausal endings (rubāk, yabīd) are written as the vocalised text has them.
line 1.5: 'hawāk' is 'your air, your breeze'; the same word also means 'love of you', and both senses may be meant.
line 1.9: al-Simāk is the Arabic name of bright stars (Arcturus and Spica); 'reaching al-Simāk' means reaching the heights of the sky.

line 2.2: 'hammuhu an yastaqilla' can be read 'their care is to be independent' (the youth themselves) or 'that you be independent'; the subject of yastaqilla is the youth's aim, the homeland's freedom.
line 2.4: 'nastaqī mina al-radá', literally 'we draw water from death', i.e. we will drink death rather than be enslaved.
line 3.8: 'yā hanāk' is an exclamation of wished happiness, 'how blessed you are'.
